english-literature.anth-open-power.0006.all: Half-caste: speaker defies the powerful figure, the person who uses the term, subverts via irony; compare with e.g. The Tyger (creator as powerful) or La Belle Dame (powerful femme fatale).

english-literature.anth-open-power.0016.all: The Tyger (Blake): creator imagery, blacksmith metaphors 'hammer', 'chain', rhetorical questions, rhymed couplets, regular trochaic rhythm, control/awe at creation; compare with e.g. Prayer Before Birth or War Photographer for control.

english-literature.anth-pair-advice.0006.all: Do not go gentle: instruction to father to resist death, villanelle; Half-caste: speaker demands to be treated as equal; both address imperative/advice but differ in tone, form (strict villanelle vs free verse dialect).

english-literature.anth-pair-advice.0005.all: Both about speakers' beliefs about death: Thomas defiant/rage, Rossetti accepting; sonnet vs villanelle; imperatives in both.

english-literature.anth-pair-death.0010.all: War Photographer (Duffy): photographer develops photos of dead; end of life in war; Poem at Thirty-Nine: father's death remembered; both about those who die, different focus: public vs private. Quatrains/rhyme vs free verse.

english-literature.anth-pair-death.0011.all: Poem at Thirty-Nine: daughter's loss of father, ordinary language; La Belle Dame: knight's near-death, knights in thrall to enchantress, death-pale warriors; ballad quatrains vs free verse.
